mainTopic: Work on חול המועד: contractors, animals and fields, preventing a loss, and the nature of the laws of the מועד
overview: The amud opens with שמואל's rule that non-Jewish contractors may not do a Jew's job inside the תחום on forbidden days, but may do it outside. רב פפא and רב משרשיא narrow this: it is allowed only where no town is nearby, and only on שבת and יום טוב, not on חול המועד. The גמרא tells of a mansion built for מר זוטרא that the rabbis would not enter, and explains why: either an important person is stricter, or he helped the workers with straw. Next come rulings and ברייתות about work on חול המועד: unpaid bath attendants, taking on contract work for after the festival, breeding animals, and penning a flock to fertilize a field. On the flock question, רב יוסף rules like רבי's three levels of favor, food, and pay. A new משנה follows about wine in the pit. There רבי יוסי lets the owner finish the job as usual to prevent a loss, while רבי יהודה allows only covering the pit. רב יוסף rules like רבי יוסי, and the גמרא extends this to sealing a beer barrel. Finally רב compares the laws of חול המועד to the laws of כותים, since you cannot learn one ruling from another. אביי begins a comparison to the laws of שבת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל's basic rule for contractors
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says contractors working for a Jew is forbidden inside the תחום and permitted outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: contractors, inside the town limit, it is forbidden. Outside the town limit, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a basic rule about non-Jewish contractors doing a Jew's job on a day when work is forbidden: it depends on where the work is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A contractor is paid for the finished job, so he picks his own work days. Still, if Jews see the work being done near town, it looks like the Jew is having work done that day. Far away, outside the תחום, nobody sees it, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Contractors who take on a whole job and are paid when it is finished, not by the day
The limit around a town that a person may walk to on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base rule. The next two steps each make the permission outside the תחום smaller.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Contractors (who take on a job for a set price),
within the limit, it is forbidden.
Outside the limit, it is permitted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Contractors may not work for a Jew inside the תחום on forbidden days; outside the תחום it is permitted.

steps.title: רב פפא: only if no town is nearby
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits שמואל's permission: outside the תחום is allowed only when no other town is close to the work site.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even outside the limit, we only said it is allowed when there is no town close to there. But if there is a town close to there, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a condition to שמואל's rule: even outside the תחום, the work is allowed only if no other town is near the work site.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the permission was that no Jew would see the work. If another town is close by, people from that town may see it, so the reason is gone and the work is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (a phrase that narrows an earlier rule)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And even outside the limit,
we said it only
when there is no town that is close to there,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִיכָּא מָתָא דִּמְקָרְבָא לְהָתָם — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but if there is a town that is close to there, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ חוּץ לַתְּחוּם לֹא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows שמואל's permission outside the תחום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside the תחום is permitted only when no other town is nearby; if one is, it is forbidden.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: only on שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא adds that even with no nearby town, it is allowed only on שבת and יום טוב, not on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: And even when there is no town close to there, we only said it is allowed on שבת and יום טוב, when people do not usually go there. But on חול המועד, when people usually come and go there, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא adds a second condition: even with no nearby town, the permission is only for שבת and יום טוב, not for חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת and יום טוב Jews cannot travel past the תחום, so nobody passes the work site. On חול המועד people travel freely, so they will pass by and see the work, which makes it forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת days and festival days, when travel past the תחום is not allowed
The middle days of a festival, when travel is allowed

steps.confusionAlert: This does not make חול המועד more strict than שבת in general. It just means that on חול המועד people travel and will see the work, so the reason for allowing it is missing.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule is now: contractors may work for a Jew only outside the תחום, only where no town is nearby, and only on שבת or יום טוב, never on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לֵיכָּא מָתָא דִּמְקָרְבָא לְהָתָם נָמֵי,
phrases.english: And even when there is no town close to there,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וּבְיָמִים טוֹבִים,
phrases.english: we said it only on Shabbatot and Festivals,
when people do not usually go there,
but on the intermediate days of a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: דִּשְׁכִיחִי אִינָשֵׁי דְּאָזְלִי וְאָתוּ לְהָתָם — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: when people usually come and go there, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לֵיכָּא מָתָא דִּמְקָרְבָא לְהָתָם נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the permission further, on top of רב פפא's condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The permission outside the תחום applies only on שבת and יום טוב; on חול המועד it is forbidden because people travel there.

steps.title: The mansion built for מר זוטרא
steps.stepSummary: Contractors built a mansion for מר זוטרא outside the תחום; רב ספרא and רב הונא בר חיננא visited but would not go into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן, contractors built a mansion outside the limit. רב ספרא and רב הונא בר חיננא came by, and they did not go into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a mansion contractors built for מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן outside the תחום, and how two visiting rabbis refused to enter it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the building was outside the תחום, the visiting rabbis treated it as built in a forbidden way. Their refusal to enter shows how seriously they took the limits on contractors working for a Jew.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman:
they built a mansion for him,
contractors, outside the limit.

phrases.aramaic: אִיקְּלַע רַב סָפְרָא וְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Safra and Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana happened to come,
and they did not go into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בְּנוּ לֵיהּ אַפַּדְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life case showing the rule about contractors in action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rabbis would not enter a mansion built by contractors outside the תחום, treating it as built in a forbidden way.

steps.title: Some say מר זוטרא himself never entered
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the story says מר זוטרא himself also did not go into the mansion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: he too did not go into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the story: not only the visitors, but מר זוטרא himself also stayed out of the mansion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the owner also accepted that the building was put up in a forbidden way. So he gave up using his own new mansion, which shows an even stronger stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; there is another version

steps.whatToRemember: The story shows the rule being applied strictly: a building put up by contractors when it was not allowed was avoided by the rabbis, and in one version even by its owner.

phrases.english: And some say:
he too did not go into it.
phrases.notes: "He" is מר זוטרא, the owner of the mansion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the same story, making it stronger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, the owner himself also refused to enter the mansion.

steps.title: Why avoid the mansion if שמואל permits it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story of מר זוטרא's mansion using שמואל's rule that contract work outside the תחום is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But שמואל said that contractors are forbidden inside the תחום and permitted outside it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that the חכמים refused to enter the mansion. שמואל's rule says this kind of work outside the תחום is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mansion was built outside the תחום by contractors, exactly the case שמואל permits. So why act as if something wrong was done? The גמרא wants to know what made this case different.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (opens a challenge from a known statement)
Contractors, workers paid for the whole job, not by the day
The שבת boundary around a town

phrases.english: But didn't Shmuel say:
phrases.notes: This is the same rule we saw back in Step 1.

phrases.english: Contractors:
inside the boundary, it is forbidden;
outside the boundary, it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the behavior described in Steps 4 and 5 using the rule from Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The refusal of the חכמים (and of מר זוטרא) to enter the mansion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל permits contract work outside the תחום, and the mansion was outside the תחום, so there was no reason to avoid it.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: An important person holds himself to a stricter standard.
steps.simpleTranslation: An important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the law really is permitted. But an important person should be stricter than the basic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule stays fully in force. The refusal to enter was extra care because of who was involved, since people watch what important people do.

keyTerms.meaning: A set phrase: a leader must act more strictly than the basic law

phrases.english: An important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the person: same law, stricter personal standard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the work was permitted, there was no reason to avoid the mansion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The work was permitted, but an important person is stricter with himself.

steps.title: He helped them with straw
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: מר זוטרא helped the workers by supplying straw, so this was not a plain contract job.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: he gave them help with straw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the same question. מר זוטרא helped the workers with straw for the building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's permission covers contractors who work completely on their own. Once the owner is involved and helps, the job looks like his own work, so the permission no longer clearly applies.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (introduces another version)

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
He actually helped them with straw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 6, instead of the answer in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: not a true contract job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: This was a plain contract job, which שמואל permits outside the תחום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner helped with straw, so the workers were not fully independent and the permission does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for the mansion: (1) an important person is stricter, or (2) the owner helped, so it was not a true contract job.

steps.title: Unpaid bath attendants on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא allowed the ריש גלותא's bath attendants to work for the household on חול המועד, because they were not paid and were just doing a favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא allowed the bath attendants of the ריש גלותא's house to work for them on חול המועד. He said: since they don't take pay, they are just doing him a favor, and we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about work on חול המועד. רב חמא allowed it because the workers took no money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What made this work a problem was that it was a paid job. Without pay, it is just a favor to the ריש גלותא, not real work, so רב חמא saw no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, head of the Jews in Babylonia
חול המועד, the middle days of the festival
Doing a favor (literally, making someone well-liked)
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: Rav Chama permitted
the bath attendants of the Exilarch's house
to do work for them
on the middle days of the festival.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: כֵּיוָן דַּאֲגַר לָא קָא שָׁקְלִי,
phrases.english: He said: Since they do not take pay,
they are just doing him a favor,
and we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the mansion story to a new ruling about work on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unpaid work done as a favor for the ריש גלותא is permitted on חול המועד.

steps.title: Taking on contract work during the מועד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: contract work may be accepted during the מועד to be done afterward, but not done during the מועד. Whatever a Jew may do himself, he may ask a גוי to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: contract work may be taken on during the מועד to be done after the מועד, but doing it during the מועד is forbidden. The general rule is: whatever he may do himself, he may tell a גוי to do, and whatever he may not do himself, he may not tell a גוי to do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the basic rules for contract work on חול המועד. It ends with a general rule about asking a גוי to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the agreement during the מועד is fine. The actual work must wait until after. The general rule ties the two together: a גוי may only be asked to do what the Jew himself is allowed to do on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may take on contract work during the festival
in order to do it after the festival,
but during the festival it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: He means doing the work itself during the festival is forbidden.

phrases.english: The general rule is:
anything that he himself may do,
he may tell a non-Jew, and he does it;
and anything that he himself may not do,
he may not tell a non-Jew to do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of work on חול המועד with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Contract work may be agreed on during the מועד but done only afterward; a גוי may be asked to do only what a Jew himself may do.
steps.whyThisMatters: The general rule gives a simple test for asking a גוי to work on חול המועד: check whether the Jew himself may do it.

steps.title: No weekday-style measuring when taking the job
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא adds: contract work may be taken during the מועד for afterward, as long as he does not measure, weigh, or count the way he does on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: contract work may be taken on during the מועד to be done after the מועד, provided he does not measure, weigh, or count the way he does on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that adds a limit to taking on the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even just agreeing to the job has a limit. He must not measure, weigh, or count materials in the normal weekday way, because that makes the מועד feel like a regular workday.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in another source:
One may take on contract work during the festival
in order to do it after the festival,
provided that he does not measure,
and does not weigh, and does not count
the way he does on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the permission in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking on contract work during the מועד is allowed only without weekday-style measuring, weighing, or counting.
steps.whatToRemember: During the מועד: you may agree on a job for later, but not do the work, and not measure, weigh, or count like a weekday.

steps.title: No breeding animals on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: animals may not be bred on חול המועד. In the same way, a בכור and פסולי המוקדשין may not be bred.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one may not breed an animal on חול המועד. Similarly, one may not breed a בכור or פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It forbids breeding animals on חול המועד and compares this to the ban on breeding holy animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breeding animals is treated as a kind of work, so it is forbidden on חול המועד. The ברייתא adds a similar case: a בכור and disqualified holy animals may not be worked at all, so they also may not be bred.

keyTerms.meaning: Breed (bring a male to mate with a female)
A firstborn animal, which is holy
Holy animals that became unfit for the altar

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not breed an animal
on the middle days of the festival.
Similarly:
one may not breed a firstborn animal,
nor disqualified consecrated animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: breeding animals on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breeding animals is forbidden on חול המועד, just as breeding a בכור or פסולי המוקדשין is always forbidden.

steps.title: Another teaching on breeding, with an exception for a she-donkey
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא repeats that animals may not be bred on חול המועד. רבי יהודה allows breeding a she-donkey in heat so she does not cool off. Other animals are only brought in among the herd.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: You may not breed an animal on חול המועד. רבי יהודה says: if a female donkey is in heat, you may breed a male with her so that she doesn't cool off. All other animals are just brought into the herd.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא on breeding. In it, רבי יהודה adds an exception for a female donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule from step 12 stays the same: no breeding on the מועד. רבי יהודה allows active breeding only for a she-donkey, because if her heat passes she may not mate again soon, and that is a real loss. For other animals you may only put them near the males and let nature take its course.

keyTerms.meaning: That is in heat (literally, that 'asked' for a mate)
She will cool off (her heat will pass)
The herd or corral where the males are

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַרְבִּיעִין בְּהֵמָה בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: One may not breed an animal on the intermediate days of the Festival.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
A she-donkey that is in heat,
one may breed a male with her,
so that she does not cool off;
phrases.notes: He means her heat would pass without her mating, and the owner would lose out.

phrases.english: and all other animals
are brought into the herd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the ban on breeding from step 12 and adds רבי יהודה's exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breeding is forbidden on חול המועד. רבי יהודה allows it for a she-donkey in heat to avoid a loss, and other animals may only be brought into the herd.

steps.title: Keeping flocks on a field to fertilize it is forbidden on holy days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids penning animals on one's field for their manure on שבת, יום טוב, or חול המועד. If they came on their own, it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: You may not pen animals on your field to fertilize it, not on שבת, not on יום טוב, and not on חול המועד. But if the animals came by themselves, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about using a flock's manure to fertilize a field on holy days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gathering a flock on your field so their droppings improve the soil is real field work, so it is forbidden on all three kinds of holy days. If the animals wandered in on their own, the owner did nothing, so he may enjoy the benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Penning animals on a field so their manure fertilizes it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not pen animals on a field for their manure,
not on Shabbatot, nor on Festivals,
nor on the intermediate days of the Festival.
But if they came on their own, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from breeding animals to using animals to fertilize a field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Penning animals to fertilize a field is forbidden on שבת, יום טוב and חול המועד, but it is allowed if they came on their own.

steps.title: No helping the shepherds, unless they were hired long-term
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Even when the flock came on its own, the owner may not help the shepherds or give them a helper to spread the flock over the field. If the shepherds were hired for a long period, he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you may not help them, and you may not give them a watchman to move their sheep around. If they were hired by the week, the month, the year, or the seven-year period, you may help them and give them a watchman to move their sheep around.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and sets a limit: even if the flock arrived by itself, the field owner may not actively help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Helping the shepherds spread the sheep around would be the owner's own effort to fertilize his field, so it is forbidden. If the shepherds were hired for a long stretch, the work is not tied to the holy day itself, so helping them is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To move their sheep around (spreading the flock across the field)

steps.confusionAlert: Here שַׁבָּת means a week and שָׁבוּעַ means a seven-year cycle. Don't read שָׁבוּעַ as 'week'.

phrases.english: And one may not assist them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the shepherds whose flock wandered onto his field.

phrases.english: and one may not provide them with a watchman
to move their sheep around.
If he was hired by the week, hired by the month,
hired by the year, hired by the seven-year period,
phrases.notes: שָׁבוּעַ here means the seven years from one שמיטה to the next.

phrases.english: one may assist them,
and provide them with a watchman
to move their sheep around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds limits and an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not actively help spread the flock over his field on holy days, unless the shepherds were hired for a long period.

steps.title: רבי's three levels: favor, food, or pay
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that on שבת the shepherd may pasture on one's field only as a favor. On יום טוב it may be in exchange for food, and on חול המועד even for pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: On שבת, only as a favor. On יום טוב, in exchange for food. On חול המועד, for pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different approach in the same ברייתא, with a separate rule for each kind of holy day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules loosen step by step, matching how strict each day is. שבת is strictest, so no payment of any kind is allowed. יום טוב allows food, and חול המועד, the least strict, allows even regular wages.

keyTerms.meaning: As a favor, with no payment

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
On Shabbat, as a favor;
phrases.notes: He means the shepherd may graze his flock on your field only to win your goodwill, without being paid.

phrases.english: on a Festival, for food;
on the intermediate days of the Festival, for pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from the first part of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת it may be done only as a favor, on יום טוב for food, and on חול המועד for pay.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules like רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף decides the הלכה follows רבי's three-level approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The הלכה is like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף closes this topic by saying which view we follow in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two views in the ברייתא, we follow רבי's step-by-step rule. So on חול המועד a shepherd may even be paid to graze his flock on your field.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the final ruling here

steps.whatToRemember: Fertilizing a field with a flock: on שבת only as a favor, on יום טוב for food, on חול המועד even for pay. The הלכה follows רבי.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides in favor of רבי's view from step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי's three-level rule for having a flock fertilize one's field on holy days.

steps.title: New משנה: wine in the pit when something unexpected happened
steps.stepSummary: Someone's wine is in the pit and he was stopped by mourning, an unavoidable accident, or workers who let him down. רבי יוסי lets him draw off the wine, finish, and seal the barrels as usual on חול המועד. רבי יהודה lets him only cover the pit with boards so it won't sour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, if someone's wine was in the pit and mourning, an accident, or workers who misled him held him up, he may draw off the wine, finish, and seal the barrels as usual. These are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: he makes boards to cover it, so that it won't turn sour.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, about wine that could spoil when the owner was held up before the מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן links this case to the earlier משנה about olives in the press, where the same kinds of delays came up. רבי יוסי lets him finish the whole process normally to prevent a loss. רבי יהודה allows only the smallest step needed, covering the pit, with the rest left until after the מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: The collection pit next to the winepress
They misled him (workers who promised to come and didn't)
Draws off the wine into barrels
Wooden boards used as a cover

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהָיָה יֵינוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר
phrases.english: And similarly, one whose wine was in the pit,
phrases.notes: "Similarly" points back to the earlier משנה about someone whose olives were in the press.

phrases.english: and mourning befell him,
or an unavoidable accident, or they misled him,
he draws off the wine, finishes, and seals in his usual way;
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
He makes boards for it as a cover,
so that it will not sour.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהָיָה יֵינוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new case, after the ברייתות about animals and fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי lets him finish handling the wine as usual on חול המועד. רבי יהודה allows only covering the pit to keep it from souring.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the disagreement over how much work is allowed on the מועד to prevent a loss. Is it the full job, or only the minimum needed?

steps.title: Why both the oil case and the wine case are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the argument between רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה had to be taught about both oil and wine. Each case on its own could have led us to a wrong conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both cases are needed. If we only had the oil case, we might think רבי יוסי is lenient only there, because the loss with oil is large. With wine, where the loss is smaller, he might agree with רבי יהודה. If we only had the wine case, we might think רבי יהודה is strict only there. With oil he might agree with רבי יוסי. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה repeated the same argument twice, once about an olive press and once about a wine pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil is worth more than wine, so its loss is bigger. Had we seen only the oil case, we might think רבי יוסי is lenient only for a big loss. Had we seen only the wine case, we might think רבי יהודה is strict only for a smaller loss. Teaching both cases shows that each of them holds his view in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both teachings are needed)

steps.confusionAlert: "The first one" here is the earlier case of the olive press (oil). "The last one" is the wine pit case we just learned. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And it is necessary.
For if it had taught us only the first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is the earlier one about pressing olives into oil.

phrases.english: I would say that only in that case does Rabbi Yosei rule this way,
because with oil the loss is large,
but with wine, whose loss is not as large,
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Yehuda.
And if it had taught us only the last case,
I would say that only in that case does Rabbi Yehuda rule strictly,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָךְ אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: but in the other case I might say he agrees with Rabbi Yosei.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה in step 18 repeats an argument that was already taught about oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is taught for both oil and wine so we know that neither רבי יוסי nor רבי יהודה changes his view based on how big the loss is.

steps.title: Requiring a change in loss cases is not רבי יוסי's view
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבא says that any תנא who requires work on חול המועד to be done in a changed way, even to prevent a loss, does not hold like רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבא said: Who is the תנא who requires a change in how the work is done on חול המועד, even for something that will be lost? It is not רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר אבא identifies which side of the argument the strict view belongs to: requiring a change in the work even when there is a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allows the work to be done the normal way when there is a loss. So any teaching that requires a שינוי even in a loss case must follow the opposing view, like רבי יהודה's.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose view is this)?
A change from the usual way of doing the work
Something that will be lost if left alone
חול המועד, the middle days of the festival

phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak bar Abba said:
Who is the tanna who requires a change on the Festival
even for something that will be lost?
It is not according to Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the argument in steps 18 and 19 to show which view the requirement of שינוי belongs to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Requiring a שינוי in a loss case on חול המועד goes against רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that the הלכה is like רבי יוסי, so work to prevent a loss may be done the normal way on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the final ruling in the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, no שינוי is needed when work on חול המועד is done to prevent a loss. The person may finish the job in the usual way.
steps.whatToRemember: In a case of loss (דבר האבד) on חול המועד, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: the work may be done in the normal way.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument that step 20 just described.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: work to prevent a loss on חול המועד may be done in the usual way.

steps.title: May a beer barrel be sealed on חול המועד?
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רב נחמן בר יצחק whether one may seal a barrel of beer on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב נחמן בר יצחק: May one seal a barrel of beer on חול המועד?
steps.whatsHappening: A new practical question is asked about sealing a beer barrel on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only talked about wine and oil. The students want to know whether beer, which is a cheaper drink, gets the same lenient treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of the festival

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: They asked Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak:
What is the law about sealing a barrel of beer
on the intermediate days of the Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling from step 21 to a new case: beer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether sealing a beer barrel on חול המועד is allowed.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers by quoting רב יוסף's ruling that the הלכה is like רבי יוסי, which suggests sealing is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: סיני said the הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers by pointing to רב יוסף's ruling, which leans toward allowing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allows finishing the work and sealing the barrels in the normal way. So if the הלכה follows him, sealing a beer barrel should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: A nickname for רב יוסף, who knew a huge amount of Torah

phrases.english: He said to them:
Sinai said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: "Sinai" is a nickname for רב יוסף, the one who just ruled like רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 using the ruling of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, the beer barrel may be sealed.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי was lenient only with wine
steps.stepSummary: The questioners push back: רבי יוסי spoke about wine, but would he say the same about beer?
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, רבי יוסי said this about wine. But did he say it about beer?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioners challenge the answer, suggesting that beer is different from wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beer is much cheaper than wine, so losing some is a smaller loss. Maybe רבי יוסי's leniency only covers drinks whose loss is significant.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he say? (asked as a challenge)

phrases.english: Granted that Rabbi Yosei said this about wine,
did he say it about beer?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the answer in step 23 really applies to beer.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying רבי יוסי's leniency about wine to beer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wine case may depend on a larger loss, and beer is cheap, so the leniency might not carry over.

steps.title: Beer also involves a real loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי was lenient with wine because of the loss, and beer also involves a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for wine? Because its loss is great. Beer also has a loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to the reason behind רבי יוסי's leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the leniency is preventing loss, and that reason applies to beer too. So beer gets the same rule as wine.

phrases.english: With wine, what is the reason?
Because its loss is great;
beer also has a loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the same reason to the new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Beer is cheap, so leaving it unsealed is not a real loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unsealed beer barrel loses a lot, so רבי יוסי's leniency applies.

steps.title: אביי's foster mother: a small sealed barrel beats a big unsealed one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that beer suffers real loss with a saying of אביי's foster mother: a sealed six-סאה barrel is better than an unsealed eight-סאה barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אביי said: My mother told me, a six-סאה barrel that is sealed is better than an eight-סאה barrel that is not sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the claim that an unsealed beer barrel loses a lot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unsealed barrel leaks so much that a bigger barrel ends up with less beer than a smaller sealed one. That is a real loss, so sealing on חול המועד is allowed according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: Beer, like wine, counts as a case of loss, so a beer barrel may be sealed on חול המועד according to רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: As Abaye said: My mother told me:
phrases.notes: This was the woman who raised אביי, his foster mother.

phrases.english: A barrel of six se'a that is sealed
is better than one of eight that is not sealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 25 that beer also involves loss.
steps.raayaObject: That an unsealed beer barrel suffers significant loss.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's foster mother's saying about six- and eight-סאה barrels.

steps.title: The laws of חול המועד are like the laws of כותים
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא quotes רב: the laws of חול המועד are like the laws of כותים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: The laws of חול המועד are like the laws of the כותים in הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new general statement from רב that compares the laws of חול המועד to the laws about כותים. It does not yet say how they are alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from the specific question about sealing beer barrels to a big-picture statement about how the laws of חול המועד work. The comparison is puzzling on purpose, and the next step asks what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: The laws of חול המועד, the in-between days of a festival
The Samaritans, a group whose Jewish status had its own special set of rules
In halacha, meaning in how the law works

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
The laws of the festival week are like the laws of the Samaritans in halacha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the specific beer-sealing discussion to a general statement about the nature of the laws of חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The laws of חול המועד are like the laws of כותים in some way that is not yet explained.

steps.title: In what way are they alike?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what legal point רב's comparison is teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law was this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב meant by comparing חול המועד to כותים. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's comparison is too vague to use as it stands. The גמרא wants to know what practical point about the law it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What is the practical point?

phrases.english: With regard to what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רב's comparison in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What shared feature of the law makes חול המועד like כותים?

steps.title: Both sets of laws stand alone, and you can't learn one from another
steps.stepSummary: רב דניאל בר קטינא quotes רב: both are 'uprooted', so one law cannot be learned from another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דניאל בר קטינא said in the name of רב: It means that they are uprooted, and you cannot learn one from the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's comparison. In both areas, each law stands on its own and cannot be used to work out a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we can compare similar cases and work out new rulings. Here רב says that in the laws of חול המועד, just like in the laws of כותים, each ruling has no 'roots' that connect it to the others, so that kind of comparison does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Uprooted, meaning standing alone without a shared root
You cannot learn one from the other

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the laws of חול המועד are unimportant or uncertain. He is saying you cannot compare one case to another to work out new rulings.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב דָּנִיאֵל בַּר קַטִּינָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Daniel bar Ketina said that Rav said:
To say that they are uprooted,
phrases.notes: Picture a plant with no roots: each law stands by itself with nothing linking it to the others.

phrases.english: and one may not learn one from the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב דָּנִיאֵל בַּר קַטִּינָא אָמַר רַב לוֹמַר שֶׁהֵן עֲקוּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The laws of חול המועד, like the laws of כותים, are 'uprooted': you cannot work out one law from another.

steps.title: An example: sealing a jug versus sealing a barrel
steps.stepSummary: שמואל allows sealing a small jug but not a barrel, and רב דימי מנהרדעא rules the opposite, because each worries about a different concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: As שמואל said: One may seal a small jug with pitch, but not a barrel. רב דימי from נהרדעא said: One may seal a barrel with pitch, but not a small jug. One Sage is worried about loss, and the other Sage is worried about effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an example of how the laws of חול המועד cannot be worked out from each other. Two אמוראים look at the same two cases and reach opposite rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי allows the barrel because a lot of drink could be lost if it is not sealed, so he cares about preventing loss. שמואל allows only the small jug because it takes little work, so he cares about avoiding hard work on the festival. Since each ruling rests on its own concern, you cannot use one case to decide the other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to the earlier question about sealing beer barrels. It shows that each ruling on חול המועד balances loss against effort in its own way.

phrases.english: As Shmuel said:
One may seal a small jug with pitch,
but one may not seal a barrel with pitch.
Rav Dimi from Neharde'a said:
One may seal a barrel with pitch,
but one may not seal a small jug with pitch.
One Sage is concerned about loss,
phrases.notes: This is רב דימי: a big barrel holds a lot, so more could be lost.

phrases.english: and the other Sage is concerned about effort.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל: a small jug is easy to seal, so less work is done on the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל זוֹפְתִין כּוּזְתָּא וְאֵין זוֹפְתִין חָבִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the principle in step 29 that the laws of חול המועד cannot be learned from one another.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the laws of חול המועד are 'uprooted' and cannot be learned one from another.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opposite rulings of שמואל and רב דימי מנהרדעא on sealing a jug versus a barrel, each based on a different concern.

steps.title: אביי: the laws of חול המועד are like the laws of שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers a different comparison: we hold that the laws of חול המועד are like the laws of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We hold that the laws of חול המועד are like the laws of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new way of looking at the laws of חול המועד by comparing them to שבת. This is a setup line, and the explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב compared חול המועד to כותים, where each law stands alone. אביי offers a different comparison, to the laws of שבת. The amud ends here, so what the comparison means is explained on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have it as a tradition

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We have a tradition that the laws of the festival week are like the laws of Shabbos;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי נָקְטִינַן הִלְכוֹת מוֹעֵד כְּהִלְכוֹת שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different general comparison for the laws of חול המועד than רב's comparison to כותים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The laws of חול המועד are like the laws of שבת. The details of this comparison come next.
